target_customer: Large tech employers that pay to train college computer science students and interns
problem: New grad engineers need 6 to 12 months to ramp up; Edlyft offered pre-hire training and mentorship so they are productive on day one.
business_model: B2B enterprise software and program fees paid by employers

founders.name: Erika Hairston
education: Yale, BS in computer science and African American studies

founders.name: Arnelle Ansong
education: Stanford, computer science (company description on YC page)
founders.background_notes: Company description says the co-founders include former Facebook and Google engineers and a Bain consultant but does not assign roles.

exit.acquirer: Google (Edlyft AI Tutor product; YC page also names Onramp)

technical_complexity.rationale: A training and mentorship platform built on standard web tools; the AI tutor later was harder.

defensibility.rationale: Content and employer relationships could be replicated; no data or integration lock-in was described.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied it; Google bought the AI Tutor product in January 2024.

market_need_then: Employers reported long new grad ramp times, and big names such as Google, Dropbox, Tinder and LinkedIn were cited as users on the YC page.

branding.domain_note: Used edlyft.com; the site returned HTTP 503 when fetched.
branding.community_and_virality: Coverage in Black Enterprise, AfroTech, Her Campus, Forbes and TechCrunch per YC description; a YC blog interview on community.

brand_strength.rationale: Founder-led press helped awareness, but no press about the name or visual identity was found.

pivots.from: Enterprise training program for college CS students
pivots.to: AI Tutor product built through a Google Tech Exchange partnership
pivots.why: Not stated in sources I read

outcome_analysis: Edlyft sold employer-funded training for CS students, raised about 1.4 million dollars in a fall 2020 seed with Kleiner Perkins and Kapor Capital, then built an AI Tutor with Google. Google bought the AI Tutor product in January 2024, a product sale rather than a venture-scale exit. Price and the fate of the original enterprise business are not public.
notes: Seed amount, date and investors come from search result summaries of CampusTechnology (Nov 9 2020) and the YC blog; the direct pages were rate-limited and not opened. Other trackers date the seed March 2020 and list totals of 1.55M to 1.7M (unverified). A 2023 150K non-equity item appears on one tracker (unverified). Village Global and January Ventures appear only on aggregators. The acquisition is of the AI Tutor product. No competitor source dated near the batch found; CB Insights competitor pages are undated. Edlyft.com returned 503. YC status Inactive conflicts with exit type acquisition: Google bought only the AI Tutor product and the directory likely reflects that.
